title: 问路 — asking the way
summary: Finding the station. Direction words, 往 and 到, and how to ask someone to repeat themselves slowly.

lines.speaker: A
lines.translation: Excuse me, where is the railway station?

lines.speaker: B
lines.reading: Huǒchēzhàn a, nǐ wǎng qián zǒu.

lines.speaker: A
lines.reading: Qǐng nǐ shuō màn yìdiǎnr, hǎo ma?
lines.translation: Please speak a little more slowly, would you?

lines.speaker: B
lines.reading: Hǎo. Nǐ wǎng qián zǒu, dào yínháng.
lines.translation: All right. Go straight ahead as far as the bank.

lines.speaker: B
lines.translation: The station is right there on the left.

lines.speaker: B
lines.translation: Not far, ten minutes on foot.

lines.speaker: A
lines.reading: Xià yì bān huǒchē jǐ diǎn?
lines.translation: What time is the next train?

lines.speaker: B
lines.reading: Wǒ bù zhīdào, nǐ qù wènwen ba.
lines.translation: I don't know — go and ask.

vocabulary.meaning: a bit slower — the phrase to learn first
is it far? — the verb-not-verb way of asking a yes/no question

questions.explain: dào yínháng, ránhòu wǎng yòu guǎi

questions.q: Which side is the station on?
Does she know the train time?
What does 远不远 mean, and why is it built that way?
options: Is it far? — verb-not-verb makes a yes/no question
questions.explain: Repeating the adjective with 不 between is a normal way to ask a yes/no question, instead of 吗.
